secureBootWizardDesc: Secure Boot is a crucial security standard that ensures your device boots using only software that is trusted by the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM).
secureBootStep2: Press the BIOS setup key repeatedly during startup (usually F2, F12, Del, or Esc).
secureBootStep3: Navigate to the 'Security', 'Boot', or 'System Configuration' tab.
secureBootStep4: Find the 'Secure Boot' option and set it to 'Enabled'.
secureBootStep5: Save changes and reboot. The agent will automatically re-verify the status.
sshKeysWizardDesc: We detected one or more SSH private keys in your ~/.ssh directory that are not protected by a passphrase. Anyone with local access to your user account can steal these keys to gain unauthorized access to remote servers.
